newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-UKRAINE HIT BY PROBLEMS AHEAD OF CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UKRAINE HIT BY PROBLEMS AHEAD OF CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Ukraine's preparations for Saturday's World Cup qualifier against Germany have been hit by an injury crisis, ticket sale scandal and the axing of a leading player for asking too many questions.
Group nine leaders Ukraine are missing eight players through injury for the match in Kiev.
Coach Jozhef Sabo also revealed on Thursday he had excluded Hennady Orbu because "he kept asking philosophical questions during training sessions -- why should we do this or that?"
"Such behaviour creates an uncomfortable atmosphere in the team," said Sabo.
Ukrainian football federation officials have defended ticket prices of up to 50 hryvnias ($28), or a third of the average monthly salary in the former Soviet republic.
The head of the former Soviet republic's top soccer club which supplies most of the national side said he was also tired of receiving phone calls from government officials demanding free tickets.
"I am fed up with it," Dynamo Kiev president Hrihory Surkis said. "For days now I have been doing nothing but fending off phone calls from ministers and government officials asking for free tickets.
"People should learn you have to pay to see the show."
Ukraine head group nine with 13 points from seven games, followed by Germany with 11 points from five matches and Portugal with nine points from six matches.
